newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Sino-Taiwan JV bank to be launched soon.
newsitem.headline: China says Sino-Taiwan JV bank to be launched soon.

text.p: China's central bank has agreed in principle to the setting up of the first joint venture bank between China and Taiwanese business interests, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The Shanghai Pudong Development Bank had completed negotiations to set up the First Sino Bank with a registered capital of $100 million, the newspaper quoted a bank official as saying. It would be set up in Shanghai's Pudong New Area.
The newspaper did not identify the Taiwan partners, saying only that they were a group of Taiwanese businessmen registered overseas, including in the United States.
The joint venture will apply for permission to handle domestic yuan currency business, it said. Only banks based in the Pudong New Area can conduct yuan currency business.
"Since the new bank will be the first of its kind, the central bank will surely be very prudent," it quoted the bank official as saying.
The joint venture was awaiting the final green light from the central bank, the People's Bank of China, to go ahead, he said. It hopes to increase registered capital to $200 million.
Once the bank had been established in Pudong, it could set up branches in Beijing, the eastern provinces of Jiangsu and Zhejiang as well as southwestern Chongqing.
